cognate: ἀγρός = ager (*h₂éǵros), exact; πίων and pinguis from the same 'fat, swell' root (*peyH-/*peyh₂-) but different stems (Gk *piH-won-, Lat nasal/u-stem *pīngwi-)
drift_or_renewal: adjective partly renewed: Latin uses a different (and etymologically debated, possibly contaminated) stem of the 'fat' root rather than a reflex of *piHwon-
shared_syntax: attributive adjective + noun, accusative plural object of a verb (προλιπόντα ... πίονας ἀγρούς / pandere agros pinguis)
context: Both name the farmland a community holds and works: Tyrtaeus (quoted by Lycurgus) on the man who abandons his city and 'fat fields'; Lucretius on early men clearing forest to open up 'fat fields' and pastures. In Greek it is a fixed epic formula (three Homeric occurrences, same case form), in Latin the same pair in hexameter.

note: Slab dominated by Attic prose, Cato Agr., Lucretius and Edda OCR fragments; partners mostly shared common roots only. One low claim (πίονας ἀγρούς ~ agros pinguis). Leads considered and rejected as generic or not anchorable: long night(s) of love (ON Skm 42 / Catul 68.83 / Pl. Amph.), livestock lists (Xen./Hom. vs RV), raven-feeding curse (HHu I 46 vs Catul 108, no secure cognate), AVP 4.15 bone-to-bone charm (no second-branch anchor in slab), δακρύοις εἰς ἔλεον vs ad lacrumas coegi (different syntax).
